newsitem.title: USA: Biogen sees Q4 revs of $90 mln.
newsitem.headline: Biogen sees Q4 revs of $90 mln.

text.p: Biogen Inc Tuesday said it expects to report fourth quarter net income of more than $7 million on sales of about $90 million.
In a statement, the company said it also expects to report a record profit for the year of more than $40 million on sales of about $275 million.

In the year ago quarter, Biogen reported a profit of $984,000 or $0.03 a share on sales and royalties of $36.1 million. For the full year, the company earned $5.66 million of $0.16 a share on sales and royalties of $134.7 million.

Biogen Chairman Jim Vincent said between 21,000 and 23,000 patients are now taking the company's AVONEX drug for relapsing forms of Multiple Sclerosis and that between 2,500 and 3,500 patients are starting AVONEX therapy each month.
Total 1996 sales of AVONEX, which was introduced to the U.S. market in May, were in excess of $75 million.

"Biogen is moving to a solid market leadership position in the U.S.," Vincent said. "For the future, we are looking at vigorous, multi-year growth coming from expanded markets and indications. We anticipate market approval in the European Community in the first half of 1997. AVONEX recently received market approval in Israel and Switzerland and we expect to be selling in those markets by the end of the first quarter of this year. These additional approvals represent significant market potential for AVONEX."

"We will announce results of our antibody studies with AVONEX this spring at the American Academy of Neurology meeting in Boston," Vincent said. "Early data indicate there is even less antibody formation among patients on commercial drug than in the clinical trials."
Vincent said that Biogen will report more than $150 million in royalties from its licensed products in 1996, exclusive of one-time payments.

"The significance of this royalty stream to Biogen's multi-year financial performance should not be underestimated," Vincent said. "We expect this royalty base to grow in double-digits in 1997 -- and to continue to grow in the high single digits during the remainder of the decade. In financial terms, this royalty income alone is equivalent to having a proprietary drug with $600-700 million in revenues that has four-to-five years remaining before it goes off patent -- a situation common in the pharmaceutical industry."
"Combining Biogen's strong royalty growth rate with the rapid market acceptance of AVONEX leads me to conclude that 1997 is going to be a very strong revenue year for Biogen," Vincent said.
